# Hand-written test notes

Twelve claim notes written by hand for testing relation extraction, plus a
ground-truth relation list in `expected_relations.json`.

**These are deliberately NOT generated by `corpus_gen.py`.** The synthetic
corpus plants relations in shapes we control, so measuring against it partly
re-measures the fixture. These notes were written to include things the
generator does not produce, specifically:

- **Roles outside `ENTITY_CLASSES`** — a witness, a landlord, an employer, a
  public adjuster, an interpreter, an SIU investigator. None of these fit the
  closed five-value set (`claimant`, `attorney`, `medical_provider`,
  `repair_shop`, `adjuster`), so they test whether open-vocabulary extraction
  captures what the closed vocabulary structurally cannot.
- **Relations with no `CANONICAL_PREDICATES` entry** — "referred X to Y",
  "supervises", "is the daughter of", "subrogating against". The point is to
  see whether the extractor invents a sensible predicate or force-fits.
- **Casing damage** — one ALL CAPS note, one all-lowercase note, since the
  casing probe showed GLiNER is robust on recall but shifts span boundaries.
- **A quoted email chain**, so the `quoted` segment kind gets exercised.
- **Negation, allegation, and retraction**, to test whether `polarity` is
  assigned rather than defaulted to `asserted`.
- **An orphan identifier** — a phone number with no name near it.

Names, numbers, addresses and firms are invented. Any resemblance to real
people or organizations is coincidental. The NPIs are checksum-valid so the
gazetteer's Luhn check exercises its true path; the SSNs and TINs are
shape-valid only, which is all `_validate` checks for those labels anyway.

## Ground truth caveat

`expected_relations.json` is my reading of what each note says, not an
adjudicated gold set. It is good enough to catch gross failures (a relation
missed entirely, a subject and object swapped) and not good enough to report
a precision number to a client. Treat a disagreement as "look at this",
not as "the model is wrong".
